h1: The 4 Best Sharp Microwaves of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: four Sharp microwaves, from countertop to over-the-range and drawer models, compared on wattage, capacity and install type.
summary: The Sharp SMC2266KS is the best Sharp microwave for most kitchens, with 2.2 cu. ft. and 1200 watts on the counter. The SMC1162KS gives up capacity and 200 watts for a smaller footprint and price. The SMD2420MS is the under-counter drawer for accessible remodels, and the SMO1759JS is the 30 inch over-the-range replacement.
intro: Sharp invented the consumer microwave in a home setting, and it still sells the form factors most rivals have dropped: a plain countertop box, a 30 inch over-the-range unit and a built-in drawer. That range makes shopping confusing. The same brand name covers a $100 dorm appliance and a half-priced remodel project, and the installation work is the real cost difference.

A drawer oven needs a cabinet opening cut to size, and an over-range unit needs a wall mount and a vent plan. The countertop models need only an outlet. We ranked four Sharp models from their listed specs, weighing wattage, cavity volume, controls and install demands, since no sensor claim or finish matters if the unit will not fit your kitchen.

products.name: Sharp SMC2266KS 2.2 cu. ft. 1200W Stainless Steel Countertop
products.verdict: The roomiest, most powerful Sharp countertop model.
products.description:
The SMC2266KS is the Sharp to buy when the microwave is a daily family appliance. It lists 2.2 cu. ft. of cavity and 1200 watts, in stainless steel, and requires nothing beyond an outlet. Wattage sets how fast food heats, and cavity size decides whether a full dinner plate turns freely instead of catching the wall.

It earns first place because it leads on both numbers. The SMC1162KS below drops to 1.1 cu. ft. and 1000 watts, so reheating a big plate takes longer and may not fit. Against the drawer and over-range models, it avoids installation entirely.

Families heating large plates and batch meals will get the most from it, and the stainless exterior will match most kitchens. The caveat is size: it takes real counter space and sits in the $200 to $500 tier, so skip it where counters are tight.
products.idealFor: Families heating large plates and batch meals.

products.name: Sharp SMC1162KS 1.1 cu. ft. 1000W Stainless Steel Countertop
products.verdict: A compact stainless Sharp that handles daily reheating.
products.description:
The SMC1162KS is the Sharp that makes sense in a dorm or a galley kitchen. It lists 1.1 cu. ft. and 1000 watts in stainless steel and falls in the $100 to $200 tier. A 1.1 cu. ft. cavity handles soup bowls, coffee cups and typical leftovers without taking over a counter.

It ranks second because it trades 200 watts and half of the SMC2266KS's cavity for a smaller footprint and a lower price. For a single person or a pair, that is a fair exchange, as the lost power mostly shows up on large or dense dishes.

Buy it for everyday reheating where space is the limit. The caveat is the cavity: oversized dinner plates and casserole dishes may not turn freely, and the same food will take longer at 1000 watts than at 1200. Larger households should step up.
products.idealFor: Dorms and small kitchens that need everyday reheating.

products.name: Sharp SMD2420MS 24-Inch Built-In Microwave Drawer Oven
products.verdict: A drawer-style Sharp for under-counter installs.
products.description:
Sharp's SMD2420MS drawer oven solves a different problem: reach. It is a 24 inch built-in with 1.2 cu. ft., a touch control panel, sensor cook technology and under-counter installation, and it sits in the $500 plus tier. The drawer slides out at counter height, so you lift nothing above the shoulder, and the dish stays level rather than tipping out of a door.

It ranks third because the price and cabinetry requirement exclude most buyers, even though it gives a cleaner, more accessible build than any countertop here. A countertop Sharp costs a fraction of its price.

It is meant for remodels and accessible kitchen layouts. The caveat is installation: it must be planned into cabinetry, so renters and anyone wanting plug-and-play should look at the SMC1162KS instead.
products.skipIf: You rent or want a plug-and-play unit.

products.name: Sharp SMO1759JS 30 in. 1.7 cu. ft. Smart Over the Range Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A smart 30 inch over-the-range option with 1.7 cu. ft.
products.description:
The SMO1759JS replaces a worn 30 inch over-the-range microwave and frees the counter. It lists 1.7 cu. ft. of capacity, a standard 30 inch width and smart features, and it mounts to the wall above the range. The over-range position doubles as a hood, which is why venting needs checking.

It ranks last because the listing is thin: it gives no price tier and no wattage figure, while the SMC2266KS states 1200 watts plainly. Buying it means accepting that you know less about how fast it will cook. Its cavity also falls well short of the 2.2 cu. ft. countertop leader.

It suits homeowners swapping an existing 30 inch unit. Before ordering, confirm wattage and venting details, and plan professional mounting if you are not comfortable lifting it onto the bracket.
products.idealFor: Homeowners replacing a 30 inch over-range microwave.
products.skipIf: You want full wattage details upfront.

whatMatters.detail: Sharp sells countertop, over-the-range and drawer units, and each demands a different space. A drawer oven needs an under-counter cabinet opening, and an over-range unit needs a wall mount and venting. A countertop model needs only an outlet. Match the form to your kitchen layout before comparing wattage, finish or any other feature.

Wattage governs how fast a microwave heats, and a 1000 watt unit takes noticeably longer than a 1200 watt unit on the same plate. It also affects how evenly food cooks. Sharp usually prints the figure in the product title. If a listing omits it, as the SMO1759JS does, treat that as missing information rather than a safe assumption.

Cavity volume in cubic feet decides which dishes fit and turn. About 1.1 cu. ft. suits dorms and small households, while 2.2 cu. ft. takes large plates. Measure your biggest dish and compare it with the stated capacity, then check the turntable diameter on the listing so a platter actually rotates.

Sensor cook technology detects steam coming off the food and adjusts the time, which reduces overcooked edges and cold centers. It matters if you reheat a variety of dishes rather than the same mug of coffee. The SMD2420MS lists it. Look for the term in the feature bullets, not just a vague auto-cook claim.

Stainless steel resists scratches and matches many kitchens, though it shows fingerprints, and Sharp often sells the same unit in black or white. The finish letters are part of the model number, so verify the exact model before ordering. Wiping with a soft cloth keeps the exterior from scratching, and the interior needs cleaning after spills.

faq.q: Does the Sharp drawer oven need a cabinet?
faq.a: Yes. The SMD2420MS is listed for under-counter installation in a 24 inch width, so it must be planned into cabinetry. It is not a plug-and-play appliance like the SMC2266KS, so factor in cabinet work.

faq.q: What is the common Sharp buying mistake?
faq.a: Choosing by finish. Sharp sells the same model in black, white or stainless, and the letters in the model number mark the difference. Confirm the full model number, such as SMC1162KS, before ordering, because the price can differ.

faq.q: Is the SMC2266KS worth it over the SMC1162KS?
faq.a: If you heat large plates, yes. The SMC2266KS lists 2.2 cu. ft. and 1200 watts, a clear step up from 1.1 cu. ft. and 1000 watts, but it costs more and takes far more counter space.

faq.q: How do I set up an over-the-range Sharp?
faq.a: Mount the SMO1759JS on a bracket above a 30 inch range and plan for a vent path. It is heavy, so use a helper or hire an installer if you are unsure about the wall studs or the venting route.

faq.q: How do I clean a stainless Sharp microwave?
faq.a: Wipe the interior after spills with a damp cloth and use a soft cloth on the stainless exterior to avoid scratching. Wipe in the direction of the grain, and keep the vents on the SMC models clear so heat can escape during long cooking.

faq.q: Can I use the SMD2420MS on a countertop?
faq.a: No. The SMD2420MS is designed for under-counter installation in cabinetry, so it is not meant to sit on a counter. For a freestanding Sharp, choose the SMC2266KS or SMC1162KS instead.

finalTake: Buy the SMC2266KS if you have the counter for it and heat big plates, or the SMC1162KS for dorms and small kitchens. Choose the SMD2420MS only if you are building cabinetry for it, and the SMO1759JS only as a like-for-like swap for a 30 inch over-range unit, after confirming wattage and venting.
